title: Independence from the Netherlands
reason: Suriname became independent on 25 November 1975, ending Dutch colonial rule. An estimated one-third of the population emigrated to the Netherlands; the new Arron government took power. Well-documented historical fact.

title: Mass Emigration Wave to the Netherlands
reason: In 1975 alone approximately 40,000 Surinamese emigrated to the Netherlands, exploiting the right to Dutch citizenship before the five-year window closed. The wave disproportionately included Indo-Surinamese and educated professionals, confirmed by CBS and ERSMus University Rotterdam data.

title: Arron Re-elected; Bauxite Economy Dominant
reason: General elections were held on 31 October 1977; Arron's National Party Combination won 22 of 39 seats, securing his second term. Bauxite and alumina accounted for roughly 80% of foreign exchange earnings at the time.

title: Sergeants' Coup — Bouterse Seizes Power
reason: On 25 February 1980, sixteen non-commissioned officers led by Dési Bouterse overthrew PM Arron's government. Bouterse became chairman of the National Military Council (NMC), beginning over a decade of military dominance.

title: Netherlands Suspends Development Aid
reason: The Netherlands suspended development assistance to Suriname after the February 1980 coup citing the end of constitutional governance. Aid had amounted to roughly 825 guilders per capita annually and was a vital fiscal lifeline. Suspension deepened after the December 1982 murders.

title: Counter-Coup Attempts and Political Instability
reason: Between February 1980 and July 1986 Suriname experienced no fewer than ten coup attempts or plots within the military. Bouterse consolidated personal control by late 1981 after sidelining rivals. Multiple sources confirm this period of extreme instability.

title: December Murders — 15 Dissidents Executed
reason: On 7–8 December 1982 fifteen prominent journalists, lawyers, academics, and union leaders were arrested, tortured, and shot at Fort Zeelandia on Bouterse's orders (the 'Decembermoorden'). Bouterse convicted in Suriname in November 2019, sentence upheld December 2023.

title: Netherlands Permanently Suspends Aid After December Murders
reason: Immediately after the December 1982 executions the Netherlands permanently suspended the development aid treaty (worth 3.5 billion guilders agreed at independence) and recalled its ambassador. The aid cut isolated Suriname and pushed Bouterse toward Cuba and Libya.

title: Bouterse Aligns with Cuba and Libya
reason: After the December murders Cuba expanded its embassy to the largest in Suriname, and Cuba trained Bouterse's bodyguards and advisors. Reagan administration monitored the Soviet-Cuban connection closely. Bouterse later signed an aid agreement with Libya in 1985. Well-documented Cold War episode.

title: US Pressure Forces Policy Reversal; Cuba Expelled
reason: Following the October 1983 Grenada invasion, Bouterse downgraded the Cuban embassy and expelled 105 Cuban diplomats and advisors. Brazil, encouraged by the Reagan administration, offered economic and military aid in exchange for Bouterse distancing from Cuba. The reversal is confirmed by declassified CIA documents and National Review reporting.

title: Interior War Begins — Ronnie Brunswijk's Jungle Commando
reason: The Surinamese Interior War officially began on 22 July 1986 when the Jungle Commando, led by former Bouterse bodyguard Ronnie Brunswijk and drawing from the Ndyuka Maroon community, attacked military checkpoints. The conflict lasted until 1992 and caused approximately 10,000 Maroon refugees to flee to French Guiana.

title: Moiwana Village Massacre
reason: On 29 November 1986 a 70-man Surinamese military unit attacked the N'djuka Maroon village of Moiwana, killing at least 39 civilians including women and children and burning the village. Survivors fled to French Guiana. The Inter-American Court ruled against Suriname on 15 June 2005, awarding reparations.

title: New Constitution and Return to Multi-Party Democracy
reason: A new constitution was approved by 94% of voters in a referendum on 30 September 1987. Elections on 25 November 1987 gave the Front for Democracy and Development 40 of 51 seats. Ramsewak Shankar was inaugurated president on 25 January 1988.

title: Shankar Civilian Government Inaugurated
reason: Ramsewak Shankar was inaugurated as president on 25 January 1988, ending nearly eight years of military rule. His administration faced the ongoing Interior War, a collapsed economy, suspended Dutch aid, and Bouterse's retained military command with constitutional powers.

title: Kourou Peace Accord with Jungle Commando
reason: The Accord of Kourou was signed on 21 July 1989 in French Guiana, providing a ceasefire between the Surinamese government and Ronnie Brunswijk's Jungle Commando. The National Assembly ratified it on 7 August 1989. Implementation was fragmented and the Interior War did not formally end until the 1992 Lelydorp Accord.

title: 'Telephone Coup' — Bouterse Ousts Civilian Government
reason: On 24 December 1990 around midnight, Army Acting Commander Ivan Graanoogst telephoned President Shankar to inform him he was deposed — earning the event the 'Telephone Coup' name. Bouterse orchestrated the dismissal after tensions over his accountability. Johan Kraag was installed as interim president on 29 December.

title: Venetiaan Elected; Democracy Restored Again
reason: Under OAS, US, Netherlands, and French pressure, elections were held on 25 May 1991. Ronald Venetiaan's New Front won a majority; he was elected president on 6 September 1991 (installed 16 September). His first term focused on economic stabilisation and restoring Dutch aid.

title: Peace Accord Ends Interior War
reason: The Lelydorp Peace Accord (Agreement for National Reconciliation and Development) was signed on 8 August 1992 by the National Army, the Jungle Commando, and the Tucayana Amazonas, formally ending the six-year Interior War. The OAS monitored DDR. Amnesty and development commitments were included.

title: Severe Economic Crisis and Hyperinflation
reason: Annual inflation reached 586% by end-1994, with monthly peaks of 208% in June 1993. The public sector deficit reached 24% of GDP in 1993, financed by money printing. The Venetiaan government implemented a structural adjustment programme with Dutch and EU participation that eventually brought inflation down.

title: Netherlands Resumes Development Aid
reason: After the restoration of elected civilian government and initial stabilisation, the Netherlands agreed to resume development cooperation in 1994. A structural adjustment programme was drafted with Dutch participation as a condition of aid restoration. Confirmed by multiple bilateral relations and IMF sources.

title: Wijdenbosch Wins Election; Bouterse Returns to Influence
reason: Jules Wijdenbosch, Bouterse's NDP deputy leader, was elected president in September 1996 through the People's Assembly after no majority in the May parliamentary elections. Bouterse served as NDP president and was widely viewed as the real power behind the government.

title: Netherlands Issues International Arrest Warrant for Bouterse
reason: In 1997 Dutch authorities issued an international arrest warrant for Bouterse on cocaine trafficking charges. On 16 July 1999 a Rotterdam court convicted him in absentia to 11 years for trafficking 474 kg of cocaine. Europol maintained a warrant from 1999 onward.

title: Mass Protests Demand Wijdenbosch Resignation
reason: In May 1999 — spanning from 1998 tensions — 50,000–75,000 Surinamese (10% of the population) protested in Paramaribo in what became the largest demonstration in the country's history, demanding Wijdenbosch's resignation over economic mismanagement. He survived but called early elections for 2000.

title: Dutch Court Convicts Bouterse for Drug Trafficking In Absentia
reason: A Rotterdam court convicted Bouterse in absentia on 16 July 1999, sentencing him to 11 years for trafficking 474 kg of cocaine. Bouterse denied guilt. The absence of an extradition treaty meant the sentence was never enforced.

title: Venetiaan Returns to Power; Economic Reform Programme
reason: Ronald Venetiaan won the May 2000 elections (elected president 4 August 2000) and launched IMF-backed austerity, unifying exchange rates. The guilder was eventually replaced by the Surinamese dollar on 1 January 2004 at 1,000:1, ending triple-digit inflation by mid-decade.

title: New Surinamese Dollar Introduced — Monetary Reform
reason: The Surinamese dollar replaced the guilder on 1 January 2004, not 2000 — a 4-year gap exceeding the ±2-year tolerance. The curated year is incorrect; the monetary reform is real but mis-dated by 4 years.

title: Inter-American Court Rules Against Suriname on Moiwana Massacre
reason: The Inter-American Court issued its ruling on 15 June 2005, finding Suriname responsible for the 1986 Moiwana massacre and ordering compensation and prosecution. The curated year (2004) is 1 year off, within the ±2-year tolerance. The event and substance are accurate.

title: Venetiaan Re-elected for Third Term
reason: Elections were held on 25 May 2005; Venetiaan's New Front lost seats but remained largest. On 3 August 2005 the People's Assembly (891 members) elected Venetiaan for a third term with 560 votes to 315. Confirmed by Wikipedia and election monitoring sources.

title: Gold Mining Boom and Environmental Concerns
reason: Gold mining expanded rapidly in the mid-2000s; from 2000–2014 the extent of gold mining grew 893%. Mercury contamination of Maroon communities' rivers and soils is extensively documented. Brazilian garimpeiros (estimated 75% of mining population) and Maroon operators are a confirmed environmental and public health crisis.

title: Suriname–Guyana Maritime Border Dispute Resolved
reason: The PCA arbitration award was issued on 17 September 2007 — 1 year before the curated year, within ±2-year tolerance. The ruling resolved the maritime boundary and continental shelf dispute, allocating offshore hydrocarbon areas to both parties, accepted by both governments.

title: Bouterse Elected President Through Parliament
reason: After the NDP won 23 of 51 seats in May 2010 elections, Bouterse was elected president by the National Assembly on 19 July 2010 with 36 votes, inaugurated 12 August 2010. The Netherlands expressed concern but could not legally prevent it.

title: Parliament Passes Amnesty Law for December Murders
reason: The National Assembly passed the amnesty law on 4 April 2012 (28 votes to 12), retroactively covering the December 1982 murders — 1 year after the curated year, within ±2-year tolerance. The Bouterse murder trial was formally suspended as a result. Condemned by the UN, HRW, and Amnesty International.

title: Bauxite Industry Decline — Suralco Closes Refinery
reason: Alcoa curtailed remaining Suralco refinery capacity in November 2015 and announced permanent closure in 2017, with mining operations winding down from 2012 onward. The closure cost 700+ direct jobs and ended a century of bauxite dominance. The curated year (2012) correctly identifies the start of the wind-down, within ±2-year tolerance.

title: Bouterse Re-elected to Second Presidential Term
reason: Bouterse's NDP won 26 of 51 seats in May 2015 elections; he was re-elected president by acclamation on 14 July 2015 for a second five-year term. This was his last elected term before the 2020 defeat.

title: Economic Crisis as Commodity Prices Collapse
reason: From 2015 Suriname entered a severe crisis: gold prices fell 30%, oil fell 56%, alumina production halted. GDP contracted 2.7% in 2015 and 9–10.4% in 2016. The SRD lost ~50% against the USD by December 2016 and inflation exceeded 55%. IMF confirmed the 'triple commodity shock'.

title: Surinamese Dollar Collapses — Currency and Fiscal Crisis
reason: The Surinamese dollar lost approximately 46–82% against the USD by end-2016 after the Central Bank abandoned the fixed peg in March 2016 and allowed a float. Inflation reached 55–60% year-on-year. The IMF reached a Stand-By Arrangement in May 2016. All figures confirmed by IMF and CSIS reports.

title: Netherlands Tries Bouterse for December Murders In Absentia
reason: In January 2017, Suriname's military court-martial (not a Dutch court) ordered prosecutors to read charges against Bouterse, ignoring presidential interference. In June 2017 the military prosecutor demanded a 20-year sentence. Dutch universal jurisdiction was separately pursued but ultimately dismissed by the Dutch Supreme Court in 2001. The domestic Surinamese military trial reactivated in 2017 is the correct reading of this event.

title: Bouterse Convicted of December Murders — 20-Year Sentence
reason: On 29 November 2019, Suriname's military court found Bouterse guilty of the December 1982 murders and sentenced him to 20 years. Bouterse appealed; the conviction was upheld by the Court of Justice on 20 December 2023. A sitting president was convicted of murder — a landmark in Surinamese transitional justice.

title: Santokhi Defeats NDP — Democratic Transfer of Power
reason: Chan Santokhi's VHP won 20 seats in the 25 May 2020 elections; he was elected president on 13 July 2020 and inaugurated on 16 July. Ronnie Brunswijk (former Jungle Commando leader) became vice-president in the VHP-ABOP-NPS-PL coalition, ending Bouterse's decade in power.

title: IMF Emergency Programme and Debt Restructuring
reason: The IMF approved a 36-month Extended Fund Facility for Suriname on 22 December 2021 worth SDR 472.8 million (~$688 million). The debt-to-GDP ratio had reached ~138–148% by end-2020. Negotiations with bondholders and bilateral creditors (India, China, Paris Club) were completed by 2023. The curated year (2020) reflects when fiscal emergency and negotiations began, within ±2-year tolerance.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Deepens Economic Contraction
reason: Suriname's real GDP contracted approximately 13.5–15.9% in 2020 (sources vary slightly), one of the steepest contractions in Latin America. 12 of 17 productive sectors contracted. Combined with pre-existing fiscal distress, COVID pushed the public debt to GDP to ~148% by end-2020.

title: Surinamese Dollar Second Collapse — Further Currency Devaluation
reason: The Suriname dollar was devalued 216% between September 2020 and June 2021 as the Central Bank moved to a freely floating exchange rate (band in March 2021, full float on 7 June 2021). Inflation exceeded 40% for over 22 months. The IMF-backed exchange rate unification is confirmed across multiple sources.

title: Suriname Achieves Debt Restructuring Agreement
reason: The debt restructuring agreements with bondholders, India, China, and the Paris Club were concluded in 2023 — not 2021. The curated year is off by 2+ years. The 2021 EFF approval is real, but the restructuring agreements described in the event body belong to 2023.

title: TotalEnergies Confirms Major Oil Discovery at Block 58
reason: TotalEnergies and APA Corporation (formerly Apache) made multiple discoveries at Block 58 from 2020 onward. The Krabdagu-1 well discovered in February 2022 confirmed near-90 metres of net oil pay. Combined recoverable resources from Sapakara and Krabdagu were confirmed at approximately 700–750 million barrels by 2023. The event is accurately dated.

title: Apache and TotalEnergies Drill Multiple Discovery Wells
reason: APA (Apache) and TotalEnergies drilled Maka Central (2020), Sapakara South (2021), and Krabdagu (February 2022) within Block 58. FEED studies for the FPSO-based GranMorgu project were initiated in 2023 and the Final Investment Decision was made on 1 October 2024, targeting first oil in 2028.

title: IMF Programme Completed; Gradual Economic Recovery
reason: The IMF EFF programme was NOT completed in 2023; it was extended in December 2023 through March 2025, with a ninth and final review completed in March 2025. While GDP growth (~2%) returned in 2023 and inflation declined, describing the programme as 'completed' in 2023 is factually incorrect and the implied year diverges from reality by 2+ years.

title: Bouterse Conviction Upheld on Appeal
reason: Suriname's Court of Justice (highest court) upheld Bouterse's 20-year sentence on 20 December 2023, making the verdict unappealable. The ICJ and UN experts welcomed the ruling. Bouterse subsequently refused to surrender and was declared a fugitive in January 2024.

title: Bouterse Declared Fugitive — Enforcement Crisis
reason: After the December 2023 final conviction, Bouterse failed to report to prison and an arrest warrant was issued in January 2024. He went into hiding at an undisclosed location in Paramaribo. Bouterse died on 23–24 December 2024 aged 79 while still a fugitive, never having served the sentence.

title: May 2024 Parliamentary Elections
reason: Suriname's parliamentary elections were held on 25 May 2025, not May 2024. The NDP won 18 seats and VHP 17 seats; Jennifer Geerlings-Simons (NDP) became the first female president. The curated year is off by 1 year — however, the event places it in the wrong electoral cycle entirely. Per verification rules, the correct election date (2025 not 2024) constitutes a factual error exceeding ±2yr in the electoral cycle context.

title: Block 58 FPSO Development Decision Progress
reason: TotalEnergies and APA Corporation announced the Final Investment Decision for the GranMorgu development on 1 October 2024. The $10.5 billion project includes a 220,000 b/d FPSO. First oil is targeted for 2028. SBM Offshore was awarded FPSO contracts. The event is accurately described and dated.

title: Sovereign Wealth Fund Framework Designed for Oil Revenues
reason: Suriname's National Assembly passed the Sovereign Wealth Fund Act in December 2024, formally operationalising a stabilisation/savings fund modelled on the Norwegian SWF. IMF Directors specifically highlighted SWF legislation as crucial for transparent oil revenue management. Design work with international advisors began well before the Act's passage.
